verdict.rationale: Appwrite's own llms.txt calls it an "open-source backend platform," and a public GitHub repository (github.com/appwrite/appwrite) shows the source can be read. Its self-hosting docs describe running the full stack yourself on Docker, which is consistent with the source being openly available. missing for 10: the specific license is never named or quoted (e.g., which OSI license and its terms), and there is no independent confirmation of the licensing terms.
